answer: Cluster identities by funding paths and invite edges, not headcount. When one operator runs a nebula of masks from a single inference pipeline, the funding graph betrays them: it lights up as one dense umber-shaded blob with a shared origin wallet, overlapping vouchers, and synchronized bidding. The protocol caps reward emission per cluster and makes each agent lock its own aged vault of stake from an independent source. So cheap masks stop paying: every extra identity needs separate capital, a distinct human voucher, and time to age, so cost scales with resources per identity, not per signup.
